motion: Did Jesus rise from the dead?

bridges.description: Early Jerusalem-linked proclamation supplies the historical starting point for an actual appearance inference.
Costly sincerity and difficulties for alternatives connect the proclamation to a real resurrection.
Bayesian comparison allows resurrection to receive support when it predicts the evidence better than rivals.
God's redemptive purposes and Jesus's character make a unique resurrection antecedently fitting.
The extraordinary affirmative claim bears a high evidential burden and unresolved evidence warrants withholding belief.
Historical reports cannot by themselves demonstrate a supernatural cause or its causal connection.
Late, interested, and indirect sources limit access to both the original experiences and the event.
Legend, sincere error, social reinforcement, and heterogeneous causes remain live alternatives to resurrection.
Divine hiddenness and moral questions reduce the fit of the proposed theological background.

sections.title: Early testimony and historical access
sections.rationale: This section covers whether the appearance proclamation can be traced early and what that tracing establishes about the underlying event.

sections.title: Sincerity, legend, and alternative explanations
sections.rationale: This section covers the main competing accounts of the reported appearances, including sincerity, legendary development, hallucination, conformity, and the need for one or several explanations.

sections.title: Probability, method, and supernatural inference
sections.rationale: This section covers the standard of evidence, whether supernatural causation can be inferred, and the dispute between Bayesian comparison and methodological restraint.

sections.title: Theological fit and divine hiddenness
sections.rationale: This section covers whether God's purposes make Jesus's resurrection antecedently fitting and whether hiddenness and moral concerns count against that background.

speakerAttributionReview.audienceQuestionBoundaries: Audience premises are excluded from debater commitments. Selected audience material begins only when Giunta or Dillahunty answers or counter-responds.
speakerAttributionReview.mixedSpans: Selected spans avoid audience-only premises and most cross-talk. Reply descriptions identify the target without treating an opponent's words as the selected speaker's commitment.
speakerAttributionReview.rationale: All selected moves use named or uninterrupted turns with source-specific contextual support; no selected move contains a material unresolved ownership ambiguity requiring an audio check.

selectionBalanceAudit.rationale: Selection follows distinct burden-bearing moves and reply duties. Any small asymmetry reflects the recording's distribution of independent claims rather than a target count.
